title: Greg Banks Interview: The New Orleans Singer Who Went From NYC Subway Platforms to the World Stage
excerpt: The New Orleans-born, Brooklyn-based singer-songwriter on Katrina, 40 million street-performance views, a viral moment that reunited a family, Lenny Kravitz, and taking his music global.

title: MIDDEKO Interview: The Faceless Baltimore Rapper Building a Y2K, Visual-Kei World
excerpt: The Baltimore-area alt-rap artist keeps his face out of frame so the music, characters and art can speak first. He talks FALLINLUV, the upcoming SAMEWAY, and a DMV scene with no single lane.

title: Howard R. Carr and the Long View: A Painter's Decades Come Into Focus
excerpt: Months after we first profiled him, painter Howard R. Carr has drawn coverage from Washington to Italy and India, and now joins a new online exhibition built around what time teaches an artist about how to see.

title: Four Senators Reach a Bipartisan Deal to Speed Up Energy Projects and Make Data Centers Pay Their Share
excerpt: Sens. Heinrich, Lee, Capito, and Whitehouse, from both parties, introduced the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act to speed up energy permitting and force data centers to pay for the grid upgrades they require.

title: Durbin Meets With State Department to Protect Global Water Programs After USAID Cuts
excerpt: Sen. Dick Durbin met with Assistant Secretary of State Wesley Brooks to press the case for global water and sanitation programs, warning the world's poorest could be overlooked after the Trump administration gutted USAID.

title: Stillness in Action: Howard R. Carr's Half-Century in the Georgetown Studio
excerpt: The Washington painter's record runs from Govinda Gallery's earliest years to the studio he still keeps at the Jackson Art Center, five decades of paint, feathers, and steady work.

title: Vote Influencers Names Rep. Al Green Its 2026 HBCU Achiever of the Year in D.C.
excerpt: The 3rd Annual HBCU Achiever Awards named U.S. Rep. Al Green its 2026 Achiever of the Year and honored eight leaders across politics, advocacy, media and business at Kitchen + Kocktails in Washington.

title: Public Housing as a Launching Pad for This UMD Pre-Med Student
excerpt: Keira Dempsey grew up in Housing Opportunities Commission housing. Its scholarships, STEM programs and mentors helped put the University of Maryland sophomore on a path toward becoming a surgeon.

title: Viola Davis, Ilhan Omar and a 50-Year Legacy Light Up the Phoenix Awards
excerpt: The Congressional Black Caucus Foundation marked 50 years of the Phoenix Awards with a night of star power and resolve in Washington.

title: They're Gen Z, and they'd like you to look up from your phone
excerpt: Two teenage sisters built ShareAScan to turn what you wear into a conversation starter - and funded it with babysitting money. Now their product is headed for the Emmy gift bags.

title: Editor's Note: An Open City, and Why Local Coverage Matters Now
excerpt: For the first time in a generation, Washington is choosing new leaders up and down the ballot. Our commitment is simple: cover the District closely, and for the people who live here.
